movement_source: row 'Net interest margin (%)', column 30 Jun 24 (Full Year Ended) -> column 30 Jun 25 (Full Year Ended)
headline: CBA's Group net interest margin rose 9bps to 2.08% in FY25 from 1.99% in FY24 (KPI table, cash basis; same row and change also printed in the Net Interest Income note and the NIM appendix, where Group interest spread widened to 1.46% from 1.40% and the interest-free liabilities/equity benefit to 0.62% from 0.59%). Most of the gain is optical: a 7bps benefit from a reduction in lower yielding liquid assets (5bps; average liquid assets down $27bn or 14% after RBA TFF repayment) and institutional pooled facilities (2bps), which the bank says has "a broadly neutral impact on net interest income". Excluding that mix effect, margin rose only 2bps, as higher capital and replicating-portfolio hedge earnings (+9bps) more than offset a 7bps drag from increased deposit price competition. Asset pricing and portfolio mix were flat, basis risk -1bp, Treasury and Markets +1bp. NII rose $1,199m or 5% to $24,023m.

drivers.columns: Jun 25 Full Year vs Jun 24 Full Year
drivers.narrative: Reduction in lower yielding liquid assets (+5bps) and institutional pooled lending facilities (+2bps); average liquid assets fell $27bn or 14% to $172bn "following repayment of the RBA Term Funding Facility". CBA stresses these have "a broadly neutral impact on net interest income", so ex-this the margin rose only 2bps.

drivers.columns: Jun 25 Full Year vs Jun 24 Full Year
drivers.narrative: "Increased margin by 9 basis points driven by the net impact of the replicating portfolio due to changes in portfolio rate and volume (up 5 basis points) and higher earnings on capital hedges (up 4 basis points)." The Highlights page attributes the underlying 2bps improvement primarily to these capital and replicating portfolio hedges.

drivers.columns: Jun 25 Full Year vs Jun 24 Full Year
drivers.narrative: "Funding costs: Decreased margin by 7 basis points driven by increased deposit price competition." Highlights repeats that the underlying 2bps gain was "partly offset by the impact of increased competition on deposit pricing". No split between deposit and wholesale components is disclosed for the full year.

drivers.columns: Jun 25 Full Year vs Jun 24 Full Year
drivers.narrative: Basis risk "arises from the spread between the 3 month bank bill swap rate and the 3 month overnight index swap rate. The Bank's margin decreased 1 basis point reflecting an increase in the average spread."

drivers.columns: Jun 25 Full Year vs Jun 24 Full Year
drivers.narrative: "Treasury and Markets: Increased margin by 1 basis point." The bank discloses no further reason for this contribution.

drivers.columns: Jun 25 Full Year vs Jun 24 Full Year
drivers.narrative: "Asset pricing: Flat." A published zero bar: lending margins/competition contributed nothing to the FY25 movement, despite home loan average balances rising $22bn or 4% to $598bn and business and corporate loans $12bn or 4% to $272bn. No further reason disclosed.

drivers.columns: Jun 25 Full Year vs Jun 24 Full Year
drivers.narrative: "Portfolio mix: Flat." A published zero bar for the full year comparison; the bank gives no reason. (Separately, in the half-on-half walk portfolio mix added 1bp on favourable asset mix from business lending growth — a different comparison.)

notable_items: The 7bps liquids & pooled facilities benefit is a mix effect the bank describes as having a broadly neutral impact on net interest income; CBA's own 'underlying' margin measure is +2bps.
limitations: Only the FY25 profit announcement publishes the FY24->FY25 NIM walk; the FY24 results presentation's Group margin walk covers FY23->FY24 (a different comparison) and so cannot corroborate the bar values. Corroboration of the 9bps movement rests on three separate tables/notes within the FY25 book plus the FY24 book's 1.99% base.
The Funding costs bar is a net number; CBA attributes it to increased deposit price competition but does not split deposits from wholesale funding for the full year.
The bank does not disclose reasons behind the zero Asset pricing and Portfolio mix bars, nor behind the +1bp Treasury and Markets bar.

evidence_records.quote: Reduction in lower yielding liquid assets and institutional pooled lending facilities drove a 5 basis point and 2 basis point increase in margin respectively.

Net interest income was $24,023 million, an increase of $1,199 million or 5% on the prior year. The result was driven by a 9 basis point increase in net interest margin to 2.08% and a $9 billion or 1% increase in average interest earning assets to $1,154 billion.
Liquid asset average balances decreased $27 billion or 14% on the prior year to $172 billion following repayment of the RBA Term Funding Facility.

Portfolio mix: Flat. Basis risk: Basis risk arises from the spread between the 3 month bank bill swap rate and the 3 month overnight index swap rate. The Bank’s margin decreased 1 basis point reflecting an increase in the average spread.
